A collector loop drains it and emits 'content-search-results' in ADAPTIVE TIME-BASED BATCHES (16ms first, then 100ms; content_search.rs:363-399). Backend caps MAX_MATCHES_PER_FILE=50 and clamps max_results to 5000.

Frontend: useContentSearch listens; ingest() fires per event (dedup, flattenBatch, publish replaces the $state.raw array). ContentSearchDialog derives rows, renders via VirtualList (already virtualized).

Batching EXISTS at the backend collector loop (primary throttle). Where stutter can still arise / batching could be added:
- Route A (backend): tune steady interval or cap batch size in content_search.rs; 100ms + up-to-5000 results means large late batches.
- Route B (frontend): publish() replaces the array every event with no coalescing; add rAF-coalesced publish (raf-coalesce.ts) in use-content-search.svelte.ts.
- Route C (VirtualList): computeOffsets rebuilds full offsets over the whole growing list per batch (quadratic); fix by incrementally extending offsets on append.

Ambiguity: fix could live at A, B, or C — all included. C scales with total rows and is the strongest candidate under a large result stream; A/B scale with event frequency. E2E can't reproduce this since mock-invoke returns inline.

Control/data flow: TilesView renders one ThumbnailImage (image or kind="video") or FolderThumbnail per file entry. ThumbnailImage is the ONLY place concurrency is bounded on the frontend: module-scoped `createPool(8)` (microPool) and `createPool(4)` (fullPool) plus an IntersectionObserver (rootMargin 200px) that only starts work for visible tiles and lets queued work bail if the tile scrolled away. On becoming visible it `microPool.acquire()` -> `getMicroThumbnail` (16x16, also pre-warms the full cache) -> `fullPool.acquire()` -> `getThumbnailData` (128x128). Results are stored in the frontend LRU blob cache (thumbnail-cache.ts) so re-scrolls avoid re-invoking. api/thumbnails.ts invokes the Tauri commands.

Backend (thumbnails.rs): each command (`get_thumbnail`, `get_thumbnail_data`, `get_micro_thumbnail`, `get_video_thumbnail_data`, `get_folder_preview`) does `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(...)` with NO semaphore and NO explicit blocking-thread cap (lib.rs/main.rs set none, so tokio's default ~512-thread blocking pool applies). The per-cache-key `INFLIGHT` HashMap<String, Arc<Mutex<()>>> (with_inflight_lock) only serializes DUPLICATE requests for the SAME key — it does not throttle distinct images. So the effective concurrency limit today is entirely the frontend pools (max ~8 micro + 4 full inflight invokes); if that gate is bypassed or a batch of distinct images is requested, the backend will run all decodes in parallel and saturate CPU.

Key nuance for a folder of thousands of images: virtualization (VirtualList) + IntersectionObserver mean only near-viewport tiles request thumbnails, and the 8/4 pools cap in-flight work — so CPU saturation typically comes from (a) fast scrolling churning many acquire/release cycles, (b) FolderThumbnail multiplying requests (folder-preview scan + up to 3 nested ThumbnailImages per folder tile), and/or (c) the pool caps being higher than the machine's core count. Thumbnails render only in Tiles view (Details/List views do not mount ThumbnailImage).

Two valid fix routes: (1) Frontend-only — tune/unify the pools in ThumbnailImage.svelte, add a shared global scheduler, or make pool size adaptive to hardwareConcurrency (files: ThumbnailImage.svelte, possibly api/thumbnails.ts, TilesView.svelte, FolderThumbnail.svelte). (2) Backend cap — add a global tokio Semaphore (sized to CPU cores) or a bounded worker queue guarding the spawn_blocking decode in thumbnails.rs, giving a hard limit independent of the frontend (files: thumbnails.rs, possibly lib.rs / task_registry.rs). A robust fix likely does both."
